review_description: It seems to me the installation guys are contractors not the Arise staff. They were not nice nor rude. Just plain.

I’ve had a terrible experience with Arise Solar. My system has never worked properly since installation, and every time I raised concerns, my cases were closed without any real action.I’m now dealing with a serious safety issue involving dangerously high voltage in my home, confirmed by a licensed electrician, and it has already damaged appliances. Despite this, I’ve received no meaningful support or urgency from Arise Solar.This has been incredibly frustrating and stressful, and based on my experience, I cannot recommend this company.I expected professionalism and accountability. Instead, I got excuses and silence. This company has left me with a system I can’t trust and safety risks no one should have to deal with. I would strongly warn others to look elsewhere.

It’s now been over two months, and I still have no confirmed installation date and no meaningful response from the company.After repeated calls and emails, I was finally told that “stock is not there,” with vague promises of a possible installation “sometime in November.” Since then - complete silence. No follow-up, no update, and no indication of when, or even if, the work will happen.This level of disorganisation and lack of communication is unacceptable for a company advertising itself as professional and reliable. I’ve had to escalate the matter to Consumer and Business Services SA just to get some accountability.

As with my previous experience with Arise this battery installation was a mix of good and bad.On the bad side the location they had quoted on was unacceptable to their contracted installer so the installer and myself had to quickly make other arrangements. Happily this was possible without much drama. The other thing was Arise had not supplied the installer with one required component for the original configuration but the change in location and configuration fixed that oversight so we got lucky there. Also on the bad side was an initial misconfiguration of the backup which caused an overload and blacked out the entire house after the installation team had left.I made some phone calls and eventually the sparky returned and rearranged some wiring which fixed the overload but did not provide the blackout protection I wanted. So we did a private deal and for a few hundred dollars he upgraded my meter box so that only the lights and one power circuit were automatically backed up but I could manually switch the other power circuits to be backed up if needed and if I was sure the load was within the capacity of the inverter. This upgrade was actually worthwhile and good value as it replaced all the fuses in my box with circuit breakers.On the good side the installation and equipment looks great and is working very well. It is an integrated Sofar system 5kW inverter and three 5.2 kW/hr batteries with a useable 14kW/hr of storage. The inverter connects with 6.6 kW of Canadian solar panels which at midday have been outputting up to 7.5 kW which the inverter handles for ten minutes or so before, I suppose getting too hot, and cutting the output back to a steady 5.2 kW. I also have an older 6kW solar system which combines with this one so except for one very overcast and wet day the battery has fully recharged by midday after falling to 10 or 20 percent overnight.The price was OK and after some discussion Arise knocked $400 off the final price as compensation for the blackout inconvenience.

Living in the far Northern New England Tablelands, we finally decided to investigate solar power (we had previously had it installed in Brisbane). We already had solar hot water. We contacted Arise and, after they sent us a satellite photo of our roof with proposed solar panels fitted, we agreed to allow them to supply and install. We paid a securing deposit of $100 with the remaining $3,800 to be paid on the day of installation. The panels etc arrived by truck at 7.30am Sunday 29th October 2023 with the installation booked to be done Friday 3rd November. We received an e-mail on Tuesday 31st October stating that the installation would now be the next day (1st November). We changed a specialist medical appointment so that we would be present (the equipment was safely locked in our garage). NOBODY TURNED UP!! They then said (the next day) that they would be there on the original date (3rd Nov). Guess what!! That's right - they didn't turn up again. This has happened five (5) times and not once has Arise notified us that they would not be here. We have had to contact them each time to find out what's happening (at one stage, we were told three (3) different stories on the same day).We have virtually put our lives on hold waiting for these "cowboys"!After the fifth time, we decided that we'd had enough and told them to come and get their equipment - that there is NO way we will ever to permit them to install their panels etc on our house. After offering us discounts etc, they finally woke up that we were "fair-dinkum" and agreed to pick their gear up - we only required notice so that we could ensure that someone would be here. A person new to us stated (we have been dealing mainly with a different customer service person) said that they were installing a system nearby on Tuesday 23rd January and that they would pick up from our residence when they delivered to the other address. NOBODY turned up!! At 2pm on Tuesday 23rd, we sent an e-mail to them stating that, once again, we were waiting - where was the truck. At 2.35pm we received a call from a very heavily-accented man (could not understand his name) who stated that he had just spoken to the truck driver who said that he had already picked up the gear from our address. I told the guy that he was talking b******t because I was standing in my garage looking at the panels, inverter etc, on their pallet, still wrapped in plastic. He stammered a bit and said that he would ring me back. HE DID NOT RING BACK!! I have since contacted Dep of Fair Trading who have advised me to envoke the "Uncollected Goods Act - 1995", and give Arise 28 days notice after which I am entitled to sell or otherwise dispose of these items. I have given Arise written notice (to expire 21st Feb) and since then, they will not return calls or e-mails.Can you imagine the trouble that we would have if we had to make a warranty claim?ARISE SOLAR - COME AND COLLECT YOUR GEAR - JUST GIVE US 24 HOURS NOTICE AS WE HAVE REQUESTED. We have tried to "fit-in" with you now for three months - we have postponed medical appointments and even delayed a holiday.TO ADD INSULT TO INJURY, ARISE HAS SENT US E-MAILS ASKING US TO RECOMMEND THEM TO OUR FRIENDS!!!!

They proved that dealing with them directly brought about a prompt resolution of my problem.I strongly recommend to anyone considering installing a solar system to go directly to Arise Solar.
